name: Fit Peptides
shipsTo: Netherlands, Belgium and other eligible EU countries
coaAccess: Public shop COA library with 25 reports across 24 entries and direct Janoshik report links. Four reports were read on the lab domain.
freeShippingThreshold: Advertised over €50 for NL and BE; over €150 for other eligible EU destinations.
dispatchInfo: The shop lists PostNL, DHL and FedEx as possible carriers. Paid orders before 16:00 on working days normally ship the same day; estimates are 1–2 working days for NL, 1–3 for BE and 2–7 for other eligible EU destinations. The dispatch location is not stated in the shipping policy.

subscore_reasons.labVerification: All four sampled Janoshik reports were read on the lab domain and name FIT Peptides as the client, but only one gives a batch identifier.
subscore_reasons.fillAccuracy: Only two reports state the nominal amount: BPC-157 20 mg measured 106.4% and Tesamorelin 10 mg measured 111.5% of nominal; the other two are excluded from fill comparison.
subscore_reasons.panelDepth: The four reports give purity and measured content, but their result sheets do not identify the purity method or show LC-MS, endotoxin, sterility or heavy-metal results.
subscore_reasons.entityTransparency: The Dutch terms identify a trade name, an Amsterdam address not open to visits and a published KVK number; neither a match in the public register nor the legal entity behind the trade name was confirmed.
subscore_reasons.dispatchReliability: The policy names carriers, a same-day cut-off and delivery estimates, but does not identify the dispatch location; no delivery was tested.
subscore_reasons.valuePerMg: Five exact single-vial variants have public regular and sale prices; this limited snapshot does not support a catalog-wide value claim.

strengths: Direct lab links led to four readable Janoshik reports with FIT Peptides named as client.
The shipping policy names carriers and distinguishes delivery estimates for the Netherlands, Belgium and other eligible EU destinations.
weaknesses: Three of the four lab reports have no usable batch identifier; two do not independently state the shop-listed 10 mg label amount.
For Janoshik report 105378, the shop-hosted image and the lab-hosted image disagree on the manufacturer field.
The legal entity behind the trade name and the dispatch location remain unconfirmed.
verdict: Four sampled reports were read on Janoshik’s own domain, but only the Tesamorelin report gives a batch identifier. Two reports state a nominal amount, and one shop copy disagrees with the lab on the manufacturer field. The Dutch terms disclose a trade name, not the legal entity behind it.
summary: Dutch research-reagent shop with a public Janoshik report library and published shipping estimates for the Netherlands, Belgium and other eligible EU destinations. The Amsterdam contact address and the Deventer returns address do not identify the dispatch location.
notes: Four reports across three compounds were checked, not the entire library and not the stock currently shipped. The shop maps reports 105378 and 109324 to 10 mg variants, but neither the lab sheets nor their attached sample photos show 10 mg. Report 105378 names the sample ‘Sample 1’ and the lab photograph identifies BPC-157; the shop copy says the manufacturer is ‘Unknown’, whereas the lab copy says ‘FIT Peptides’. The Tesamorelin report’s FP2026-10 batch is also on the shop’s copy; it was not matched to inventory. Five regular catalog variants across four product pages were sampled; no cart, pack or conditional discounts were checked. The Retatrutide link redirected to the general catalog, so it was not recorded as a product.
